tx_crazy_cat_a_k_a_palisades.blurb: A compact bouldering spot tucked into a rocky desert arroyo on the west side of the Franklin Mountains, close to El Paso. Locals use the nickname Crazy Cat for what is formally The Palisades. The roughly twenty problems are mostly in the V1 to V6 range, with one VB and a handful of harder lines, so there is something for newer boulderers and for people wanting a short, steep session. Expect overhanging blocks, roofs, traverses and a prominent prow rather than tall walls. It is a quick-hit area for the city rather than a destination crag, and the surrounding terrain is classic Chihuahuan Desert scrub and cactus.

_expect.name: Dungeons and Dragons Wall & J.R.R. Tolkein Wall

tx_dungeons_and_dragons_wall_j_r_r_tolke.blurb: Two neighboring limestone walls at Monster Rock, a sport crag west of Austin. The fantasy-themed route names match the setting: one wall lines a narrow pit shared with a second wall, while the other sits on the main cliff just beyond it. All twenty routes are bolted sport lines, from 5.6 up to a couple of 5.11s, with most sitting between 5.8 and 5.10. That spread makes these walls the gentlest part of the crag and a reasonable place to build lead confidence. The canyon setting holds cool air, which helps in warm weather. Expect a short scramble and ladders to reach the base.

ut_r_crags_two_finger_canyon.blurb: A narrow sandstone canyon in the San Rafael Swell, in the part of the Swell sometimes called the Sandstone Alps. Walls here face every direction, so you can usually find sun or shade to suit the day. Nearly all of the 29 routes are trad, with a single sport line, and the grades run from easy fifth class up to the low 5.11s, though most are 5.8 to 5.10. Some lines are runout and rock quality can be questionable in places, so this suits climbers comfortable placing their own gear and reading sandstone. Reaching the canyon means a dirt road and a stretch of slickrock, which keeps the crowds away.

ut_maverick_buttress.blurb: The main wall of Long Canyon, a short drive from Moab off the Potash Road. Splitter sandstone cracks dominate, nearly all of them gear-protected single pitches with fixed anchors at the top. The grades are stiff for a beginner: about eight lines in the 5.10s, a big group of 5.11s, and several 5.12s. Because the face looks east, mornings are bright and afternoons cool off in shade, and the setting has views down the canyon toward the Colorado River and the La Sal Mountains. It has the most routes in the canyon and the shortest walk, so it is a good pick for a quick crack day. A few rappels need a second rope.

ut_higher_education_ridge_west_face.blurb: A quartzite face on the north side of Big Cottonwood Canyon in the Wasatch, part of the Gully of Higher Education. Half the routes are bolted and half are trad, and many are vertical to overhanging. Grades start around 5.7 and climb to a single 5.13, with the bulk of the climbing in the 5.10s to 5.12s, so it leans toward intermediate and advanced climbers. Rock quality is less consistent than at some neighboring crags, and holds can flex now and then. Route names follow a college theme. Because the wall faces west, it warms up in the afternoon: best in spring and fall, with shade needed in midsummer.
ut_higher_education_ridge_west_face.parking_note: Use the big pull-out just east of the ridge on the canyon road, which fits about a dozen cars; a smaller dirt pull-out across the road from the gully takes a few more.

ut_mine_cart_area.blurb: A roadside bouldering zone in the Left Fork of Joe's Valley, central Utah, named for an old ore cart parked beside a boulder. The sandstone here is the textured, skin-friendly Joe's variety, and the problems stretch from easy V1s to V11, with the thickest cluster in the V2 to V5 range plus a good number of harder sit starts. The main boulder faces the river, and another group sits up on the hillside via a short trail, including a cave. Walks are brief, which makes it easy to string several blocks together. The stone is weak when damp, so give it a few dry days after any moisture before you pull on.
